summary: Reviewed the booking form idempotency, availability-search threading, London date handling, robots/redirect changes, and event redirect behavior through a security and data-integrity lens. Most changes are public UX/SEO surfaces and do not introduce an auth boundary; the main residual risk is whether idempotency-key payload binding is also enforced server-side.
appears_sound: Volatile anti-bot/telemetry fields are excluded from the submit-intent fingerprint before the request body adds them, so `_t`, `turnstile_token`, and `website` changes do not force new keys in the honest client path (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1306`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1426`).

Freshly typed party size is explicitly threaded into availability and alternatives fetches instead of relying on stale React state (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:826`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:901`).

Past-date checks compare date-only strings against Europe/London today and avoid browser-local date parsing for booking validation (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:308`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:954`).

findings.description: Idempotency-key payload binding appears to be implemented in the browser only; if the booking API dedupes solely by the client-supplied key, a direct caller could reuse one key with a changed date/time/party size and cause stale booking responses or suppressed booking creation.
findings.evidence: The changed pack shows client-side fingerprinting and key selection before POST, but does not include any server/proxy code that recomputes or stores the fingerprint with the idempotency key (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1306`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1333`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1372`).
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The management API or local API route may already validate that repeated idempotency keys match the original normalized payload.
findings.what_would_confirm: Inspect the table-booking POST route and management API idempotency store to verify it rejects or reissues on same-key/different-payload requests.

empty_categories: No hardcoded secrets or API keys were introduced in the changed files.
No new raw SQL, Supabase service-role client usage, or RLS-bypassing database access appears in the pack.
No user-controlled redirect destinations were added; changed redirects are hardcoded paths only.
No new `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, HTML interpolation, or sensitive console logging appears in the changed code.
No client-side exposure of the management API key is shown; booking mutations still appear to go through the existing API/proxy pattern.
